claim.pdf_says: Format 1 (delimited):   IF condition-1 THEN statement-1 [ ELSE statement-2 ] END-IF   — with IF, ELSE and END-IF UNDERLINED and THEN, statement-1, statement-2 NOT underlined.
claim.markdown_says: IF condition-1 THEN statement-1 [ ELSE statement-2 ] END-IF   (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 27465 — no <u> markup on any word)
claim.why_it_matters: Per 5.2.6.2 an underlined word in a general format is a REQUIRED word and a non-underlined uppercase word is an OPTIONAL word. This figure mixes both: IF / ELSE / END-IF are required, THEN is optional. With every underline dropped the required-vs-optional distinction is unrecoverable from the markdown, and a reader deriving the grammar from it cannot tell that THEN may be omitted while END-IF may not. The transcription DOES have a convention for this — 14.9.17.2 on page 660 renders '<u>GO</u> TO ... <u>DEPENDING</u> ON identifier-1' — so this is an omission, not a house style.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed against the 300 dpi render of PDF page 665 (printed folio 635) and against specs/ISO_COBOL.md. (1) PRINTED GLYPHS, Format 1: I cropped and upsampled the Format 1 line and read the rules directly. There is a short rule beneath 'IF', a rule spanning the full width of 'ELSE', and a rule spanning the full width of 'END-IF'. There is NO rule beneath 'condition-1', 'THEN', 'statement-1', or 'statement-2'. The claim's description of the PDF is exactly right. (2) MARKDOWN: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 27468 reads 'IF condition-1 THEN statement-1 [ ELSE statement-2 ] END-IF' with zero <u> markup and no accompanying figure-notes block. The quoted text is verbatim correct; only the line number in the claim is off (27468, not 27465 — 27465 is the blank line after the 14.9.19.2 heading). (3) NOT PRESENT ELSEWHERE: the entire page-665 slice (lines 27450-27493) carries no <u> tags and no prose stating which words are required, so the distinction is genuinely absent, not reflowed onto an adjacent line. (4) NOT MERE FORMATTING: the underline is normative notation, not typography. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 2631 (5.2.2 Keywords) — 'They are shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats. They are required...' — and line 2644 (5.2.3 Optional words) — 'shown in uppercase and not underlined ... They may be written to add clarity'. Dropping it changes what the format means. (5) NOT HOUSE STYLE: the transcription carries 156 <u> occurrences across 97 lines, including many Chapter 14 statement formats (ACCEPT 25253, COMPUTE 26207, EVALUATE 26821-26824, EXIT 27036, GO TO 27291/27295, INITIATE 27726, INSPECT 27777-27789, ROLLBACK, SUPPRESS, VALIDATE, and the intrinsic-function formats). I verified the claim's cited counter-example: lines 27291 and 27295 fall between the page-660 anchor (27271) and the page-661 anchor (27316) under heading '### 14.9.17.2 General formats', exactly as claimed. The transcription also has a second convention for the same information — 'Figure notes' blockquotes that name the underlined words in prose (e.g. line 4318). Page 665 uses neither. The omission is therefore an inconsistency in the transcription, not a deliberate uniform policy. (6) CONSEQUENCE IS CONCRETE: a reader building a grammar from the markdown Format 1 sees four bare uppercase words with only '[ ... ]' marking the ELSE phrase, and has no way to learn that THEN is omissible while END-IF is mandatory in the delimited format. That is a real, grammar-affecting loss. Verdict: real, severity normative as claimed.
verdict.corrected_description: CONFIRMED, with three corrections and one broadening. (a) Line reference: the markdown Format 1 line is specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 27468, not 27465. (b) Citation: the underlined-equals-required rule is 5.2.2 (Keywords) together with 5.2.3 (Optional words), not 5.2.6.2 — 5.2.6 is 'Options', which governs brackets/braces/ellipses instead. (c) Scope: the defect is NOT confined to Format 1. Format 2 (historic) on the same page has the identical problem — the PDF prints 'IF' underlined, 'THEN' NOT underlined, 'ELSE' underlined, and 'NEXT' and 'SENTENCE' underlined in BOTH stacked alternatives, while markdown line 27472 ('IF condition-1 THEN { statement-1 / NEXT SENTENCE } [ ELSE { statement-2 / NEXT SENTENCE } ]') carries no <u> markup at all. So 14.9.19.2 loses the required/optional distinction in both of its general formats, dropping seven distinct underlines across the two figures (IF, ELSE, END-IF in Format 1; IF, ELSE, NEXT, SENTENCE in Format 2). Everything else in both figures — word order, bracket and brace structure, the '/' flattening of the stacked alternatives — transcribes correctly. Fix: restore <u> markup as '<u>IF</u> condition-1 THEN statement-1 [ <u>ELSE</u> statement-2 ] <u>END-IF</u>' and '<u>IF</u> condition-1 THEN { statement-1 / <u>NEXT</u> <u>SENTENCE</u> } [ <u>ELSE</u> { statement-2 / <u>NEXT</u> <u>SENTENCE</u> } ]', matching the convention already used at lines 27291/27295.
